__comment: Grafana dashboard for the Incident Commander. Import against a Prometheus datasource scraping /actuator/prometheus. The panels are ordered by the question an operator asks first: is it spending money, is it being refused, and is it telling the truth about recoveries. Panel descriptions say what a bad value means, because a number with no interpretation is a number nobody acts on.
title: AWS Incident Response Commander

panels.title: Model spend this month (USD)
panels.description: Against the configured monthly budget. The CostGuard fails closed, so this reaching the limit stops model calls rather than producing a larger bill. Bounds LLM usage only; it says nothing about what the surrounding AWS infrastructure costs.

panels.title: Model calls refused for budget
panels.description: Non-zero means the monthly ceiling has been reached and investigations are now running without a model. Not an error condition — it is the guard working — but it is the point at which conclusions stop being produced.

panels.title: Tokens by direction
panels.description: Input dominating by orders of magnitude is expected: an investigation sends evidence and receives a paragraph. A sudden rise in input with flat output usually means evidence is no longer being truncated.

panels.title: Policy decisions
panels.description: The most important panel here. A sustained rise in denials is either a misconfigured allowlist or something proposing actions it should not be — and the two are told apart by which rules appear in the audit log, not by this graph.

panels.title: Approval outcomes
panels.description: Refusals are broken out by reason. STALE and EXPIRED are routine. NOT_AUTHORISED is not: it means someone attempted a decision they do not have the standing to make, and every occurrence is in the security-relevant audit trail.

panels.title: Model calls with no reported token usage
panels.description: Expected to be the total call count on the fake and Ollama profiles, which genuinely report none. Non-zero on a paid profile means spend is going untracked and the budget is not being enforced on those calls.

panels.title: Stage latency (p95)
panels.description: Per agent. The parallel evidence stage should be roughly the slowest specialist, not their sum; if it approaches the sum, the specialists have stopped running concurrently.

panels.title: Tool outcomes
panels.description: Split by the tool's own reported status. 'unavailable' is a recorded evidence gap, not a crash: the investigation continued without that source, and any conclusion drawn during that window is weaker than it looks.

panels.title: Recovery verification outcomes
panels.description: Only RECOVERED resolves an incident. INDETERMINATE means the metric could not be read, which is neither success nor failure — a rise in it is a monitoring problem, not a remediation problem, and reading it as either would be the mistake the four-valued outcome exists to prevent.

panels.title: Time awaiting a human decision (p95)
panels.description: Measured from approval request to decision. Approvals expire, so a p95 approaching the configured expiry window means decisions are routinely arriving too late to be usable.
